subject: Maths
title: Recurring decimals
subtitle: Fractions, Decimals and Percentages · GCSE Maths
learning_objective: I can convert recurring decimals to fractions using algebraic methods.

key_vocab.definition: Recurring decimals have one or more digits that REPEAT forever. We write a dot above the repeating digit(s): 0.3̇ means 0.333... and 0.1̇2̇ means 0.121212...

sections.title: Learning Objective
sections.content: I can convert recurring decimals to fractions using algebraic methods.

sections.title: Key Words
sections.content: Recurring decimals -- Recurring decimals have one or more digits that REPEAT forever. We write a dot above the repeating digit(s): 0.3̇ means 0.333... and 0.1̇2̇ means 0.121212...

sections.title: Method
sections.content:
Let x = the recurring decimal. Multiply by 10 (or 100, 1000...) to shift the repeating block. Subtract to eliminate the recurring part. Solve for x.
x = 0.2̇7̇ → 100x = 27.2̇7̇ → 99x = 27 → x = &frac{27}{99} = &frac{3}{11}
Multiply, subtract, simplify

Key examples:
  ✓ 0.333... = ⅓  (recurring (one digit))
  ✓ 0.272727... = &frac{3}{11}  (recurring (two digits))
  ✓ 0.1666... = ⅙  (recurring (after 0.1))
  ✗ 0.25 is recurring  (it terminates (= ¼))
  ✗ 0.333... = &frac{33}{100}  (that equals 0.33 only)

sections.title: Worked Example
sections.content:
Example 1 – one repeating digit
  Convert 0.4̇ to a fraction
  Let x = 0.444...
  10x = 4.444...
  9x = 4, so x = 4/9
  = 4/9
  (One repeating digit: multiply by 10. Subtract x from 10x to get 9x = 4.)

Example 2 – two repeating digits
  Convert 0.6̇3̇ to a fraction
  Let x = 0.636363...
  100x = 63.636363...
  99x = 63, so x = 63/99
  = 7/11
  (Two repeating digits: multiply by 100. Subtract: 99x = 63. Simplify: 63/99 = 7/11.)

sections.title: Identify the recurring part
sections.content:
Write the first 6 decimal places and underline the repeating block.

(a) 0.7̇ = 0.______
(b) 0.1̇8̇ = 0.______
(c) 0.41̇ = 0.______
(d) 0.5̇23̇ = 0.______

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
✗ 0.9̇ = 0.999... < 1
✓ 0.1̇2̇ means multiply by 100 to shift the block
✗ 0.3̇ = 3/10
✓ 0.16̇ needs 100x − 10x to eliminate the recurring part
✗ All fractions give terminating decimals
